name: Bristleback Quilboar Tusk
summary: Across the northern and central Barrens, Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are taken from slain quilboar. Mankrik gathers them as proof of slaughter and tokens of vengeance.

sections.title: Trophies of Vengeance
sections.body: Bristleback quilboar defend their territory across the Barrens against Horde expansion. Their jagged ivory tusks serve as weapons in close combat. Mankrik, a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads, lost his wife in a vicious quilboar ambush. He gathers dozens of tusks as retribution, a bloody count of the suffering he means to return to the Bristlebacks.

faq.answer: Mankrik, an orc warrior at the Crossroads in the Barrens, wants the tusks. He seeks vengeance against the Bristleback quilboar after an ambush separated him from his wife.

faq.q: Why does Mankrik want so many tusks?
faq.answer: After quilboar raiders overwhelmed Mankrik and left him for dead, he was consumed by grief and fury. Sixty tusks give him proof that the Bristleback tribe is being culled in return.
Members of the Bristleback tribe carry these tusks in the northern and central scrublands and bramble camps of the Barrens.

faq.q: Do these tusks serve any purpose other than Mankrik's vendetta?
aliases: can you craft with quilboar tusks
faq.answer: Mankrik gathers these trophies solely for vengeance. Quilboar tusks can sometimes become tribal trinkets or trade goods, but these are not put to those uses.

angles.text: The quilboar threaten the Crossroads and supply trails across the Barrens. Gathering tusks serves Mankrik's vendetta and the Horde's effort to pacify the region.
As an orc, you know the weight of blood debts and a warrior's grief. Mankrik's pursuit of sixty quilboar trophies touches a shared sense of honor.
